players.product: OSAT (incl. JCET STATS ChipPAC Korea) - package substrate buyer from Simmtech and Daeduck Electronics

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record, meetings July-September 2026; CFO Liang Zheng): the 2026 fixed-asset investment budget is about RMB 100 hundred million, aimed at capacity expansion (focused on advanced packaging, plus mainstream packaging capacity per customer orders) and R&D (mainly computing and automotive electronics). H1 2026 capex was RMB 47 hundred million, up nearly 80% year over year, mostly in advanced packaging, modules and test, with high-end advanced packaging more than half. It is expanding the Jiangyin high-end advanced packaging plant and announced in June a second high-end advanced packaging plant in Shanghai Lingang; capacity is being expanded this year with a larger release next year. At the Lingang automotive plant new capacity quickly reached full load, and because demand exceeded expectations the company added automotive-grade wafer-level packaging capacity there, expected to start production next year.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 fixed-asset investment budget ~RMB 100 hundred million; H1 2026 capex RMB 47 hundred million (+~80% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): the company is optimistic on the cycle, driven by long-term structural change from AI infrastructure; back-end and especially high-end packaging and test is becoming the industry's bottleneck. Domestic demand for AI has far exceeded expectations and advanced packaging demand is growing faster than expected; overseas foundries' advanced packaging projects are spilling over; AI demand in H2 will exceed H1 and advanced packaging capacity is expected to stay in tight balance for the next few years. Domestic plants are running at full load while new capacity is validated; utilization at the overseas STATS ChipPAC plants will rise further in H2 with the mix shifting toward data centers; the company has a price-linkage mechanism with increasing customer acceptance. The Korea plants are being transformed toward AI, with the two Korean plants' resources integrated; results are expected to show clearly from H2 2026 through the next two years, extending their end markets from communications to AI compute, power and storage.

Management (IR record) outlook: gross margin, which improved in H1 on high utilization, cost control and better recognition of packaging-and-test value, is expected to keep rising in H2 as domestic plants stay full and STATS ChipPAC enters its relatively strong season and shifts toward data-center business; the selling and administrative expense ratio is expected to be lower in H2 than in H1 as revenue grows (Q2 expenses already fell from Q1, with the Lingang and JCET Microelectronics plants ramping well); the R&D expense ratio has stayed above 5% and is trending up.
